claims.text: A combined high-throughput CALPHAD, molecular-dynamics, and experimental-calibration approach can determine fusion and liquid-phase properties across the high-entropy-alloy family.
Combining CALPHAD, molecular dynamics, and in situ experiments is accurate and efficient.
The target materials are near-equiatomic, simple-solid-solution BCC or FCC high-entropy alloys.
CALPHAD high-throughput screening can predict phase-stability trends in high-entropy alloys.
Molecular-dynamics simulations can capture atomic interactions and liquid dynamics relevant to melting.
In situ STEM heating combined with molecular dynamics can reveal thermally induced structural and chemical evolution and melting behavior.
Experimental observations can calibrate or improve the accuracy of thermodynamic models and databases.
Experimental calibration ensures that complex multielement interactions are correctly captured.
Atomic-scale disorder determines mixing entropies and enthalpies and thereby governs phase transitions and liquid properties.
Relevant measurements and simulations generally need to span room temperature to approximately 1400 K or higher.
The method can determine melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, volume change at melting, and other liquid-phase properties.
Predicted fusion properties will be accurate to approximately ±5% relative to high-precision experiments.
Predicted melting temperatures will be accurate to approximately 50 K.
The combined approach will be more accurate and efficient than DSC-only or simulation-only approaches.
The method is robust for homogeneous bulk high-entropy alloys that undergo a single-step melting transition.
Nanostructuring and surface phenomena can significantly alter high-entropy-alloy melting behavior and limit the method's applicability.
Current molecular-dynamics potentials may not fully capture long-range liquid structure and kinetic phenomena.
Failure by more than ±5%, or by more than approximately 50 K for melting temperature, in at least three independent alloy compositions would falsify the approach.
